newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bellwether Cetes rate falls on good demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bellwether Cetes rate falls on good demand.

text.p: Mexico's one-month treasury bill rate fell slightly at Banco de Mexico's primary Cetes auction on Monday, as strong demand kept a lid on any rate hikes, analysts said.
At the auction this week the one-month Cetes rate fell 12 basis points to 27.25 percent.

The result was better than expected, as a Reuters survey of money market traders earlier in the day showed they had expected bellwether 28-day Cetes to be assigned at 27.55 percent, or a gain of 28 basis points from last week's rate.
Demand was 10.74 billion pesos compared with the 3.3 billion on offer, for a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.25.
"Strong demand going in to the holiday and the strong peso kept a lid on rates," said MMS International in a report.
Demand on the one-month paper has weakened at 1.847 billion pesos, compared with the 900 million pesos on offer.
Investors had been worried about the prospects of higher inflation in December and January. These worries had caused the one-month rate to rise at the two previous auctions.

Fears of higher inflation seemed to be borne out, when Banco de Mexico said earlier on Monday that the consumer price index rose 2.34 percent in the first half of December from the last two weeks of November.
Much of the sharp increase was due to the nationwide hikes in gasoline prices, and by higher public transport costs in the Mexico City metropolitan area.

"This shows that the annual inflation rate will be larger than forecast by the government and means real rates will be more negative than usual for December," said one analyst, who declined to be identified.
The inflation results were released after the bidding process at the auction closed.
The rate on the three-month paper fell 30 basis points to 26.55 percent, on the expectations that inflation will fall in Mexico after the first part of the year.
The six month paper showed a tiny decline of two basis points to 25.60 percent.
The yield on one-year paper was 25.75 percent compared with 25.68 percent the week before.
Investors have been shunning Mexican long-term paper as it will come due after the key and hotly-contested mid-term elections planned for next year in Mexico.
The auction was moved forward by one day because of the Christmas holiday.
